title: Inbound model contract and experimental pin policy for open weights
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we scale acceptance of community/open model weights, runtime teams and infra are seeing an uptick in incompatible submissions (tokenizer mismatches, nonstandard KV cache shapes, unexpected attention patterns) that cause runtime errors or silent quality regressions. Current intake guidance is high-level and inconsistent between intake reviewers. This ticket defines a concrete inbound model contract (what artifacts are required, metadata fields, compatibility signals) and an "experimental pin" policy for early-stage community variants so the catalog can safely route and serve them without breaking customer SLAs.

Scope (inclusions):
- Define required artifacts: model weights, tokenizer files or tokenizer bindings, model config (architecture, vocab size, hidden_size, rotary/rope flags), sample prompt set and a small eval run.
- Standardize compat metadata fields: declared seq_len, kv_layout_hint, expected tokenizer family, float format, quantization recommended profile, and compatible runtime tags.
- Define soft "experimental pin" semantics: a way to admit models into a restricted catalog channel with routing to non-critical capacity and auto-fallback to verified variants.
- Acceptance criteria for unpinned vs experimental models, plus automated checks run during intake.

Scope (exclusions):
- No changes to billing/pricing for experimental models in this ticket.
- No infra-only work such as autoscaling changes beyond routing config; those will be separate ENG tickets.

Goals:
- Reduce intake failure rate from community submissions by 60% in first 3 months.
- Ensure any experimental variant cannot degrade hosted tenant latencies beyond current SLOs.
- Provide clear deterministic criteria for when an experimental model must be pinned or rolled back.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound contract doc published in Confluence with exact file list and JSON schema for 'compat_metadata'
Intake UI/CLI validates required artifacts and rejects submissions missing tokenizer or model_config.json with clear error messages
Automated pre-service checks (unit-runner) verify sample eval throughput and raise a compatibility flag if tokenizer mismatch or KV shape errors occur
Experimental pin channel implemented as a catalog tag 'experimental-pin' and routing policy that sends traffic to a sandbox pool with capacity guardrails
Playbook describing rollback rules and escalation path is created and reviewed by Runtime and SRE
Metrics dashboard shows pre/post intake failure rate and experimental-variant error/latency delta; baseline and thresholds are documented
decisions: Adopt a minimal required artifact set (weights, tokenizer, model_config.json, sample prompts, short eval outputs) rather than full dev repos to reduce friction
Experimental pin will be opt-in at intake reviewer discretion for models passing static checks but failing full runtime sanity due to nonfatal quirks
Experimental variants will be tagged and routed to a separate non-prod-like capacity tier with strict QPS and tail-latency caps
Soft pin semantics: experimental models can be unpinned after 2 successful canary windows (48h each) with no regressions, otherwise require formal pin review
open_questions: What exact thresholds for the sample eval (latency and token correctness) should gate moving from experimental to verified? Runtime team to propose metrics by 2026-03-05
Should we require a minimal license/redistribution declaration from submitters for community weights? Legal input requested
How will we surface guidance for quantized submissions vs fp32—should we accept quantized weights or require reference fp32?
What marketplace policy should accompany an 'experimental' tag to communicate risk to end-users? PM/Legal to propose copy
